# Manual acceptance

Behaviour that CI cannot reach, written to be executed by a person or by an
agent driving the real GUI. The source of truth is
[`manual-checks.yaml`](manual-checks.yaml); this file is rendered from it.

```sh
yarn verify:manual stale     # which checks a pending change invalidates
yarn verify:manual sheet ID  # a run sheet for one check and its persona
```

`pass` and `fail` carry evidence. `unreached` means the flow could not be
attempted at all, and records what blocked it: a silently missing row is how
an unverified area becomes an assumed-good one.

## Personas

### 理工学系 1年生・初学期 (`undergraduate-first-term`)

Identity: undergraduate · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

First quarter of the first year. Has never used this app; signed in once
during orientation and does not remember which systems exist. Japanese
UI and Japanese school content. Uses a trackpad, not the keyboard.

Reads every label before clicking. Tries to add a course that is
obviously above their year. Expects the app to explain refusals rather
than only disabling a control. Abandons a flow that offers no obvious
next step.

### 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 (`undergraduate-senior`)

Identity: undergraduate · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

Third year, planning next quarter. Knows the syllabus site and the
timetable well. Japanese UI, mixes Japanese and English course content.
Works fast and expects the keyboard to work.

Types course codes from memory instead of browsing. Opens details in
quick succession. Adds a course that clashes with an existing one and
expects to be told which one. Uses Undo immediately after a mistake.

### 修士課程 1年・前期課程 (`masters-student`)

Identity: masters · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

First year of a master's programme, first semester. Has an undergraduate
record from the same institution that is already in the workspace.
Japanese UI. Cares about credit requirements and about 500-level rules.

Checks the grade and GPA panels first. Looks for requirements that apply
only after the first semester. Notices when an undergraduate-only count
or table is assumed.

### 博士後期課程 (`doctoral-student`)

Identity: doctoral · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

Doctoral programme, several years in. Reads the app mostly for research
scheduling and for the few courses that require doctoral registration.
Japanese UI.

Ignores the timetable and goes straight to the requirement and
registration panels. Expects doctoral-specific approval rules to be
stated rather than silently enforced.

### 編入生 (`transfer-student`)

Identity: transfer · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

Transferred into the third year from another institution. Admission year
differs from the cohort year of the courses being planned.

Looks for their own admission cohort's guidance. Notices when a guide or
requirement set from the wrong admission year is applied.

### International student (`international-student`)

Identity: undergraduate · Language: en · Device: macos-x64

Reads English better than Japanese. Sets the UI to English and the
school content to English where a translation exists. Signs in from a
laptop on the campus network.

Never switches to Japanese to decode a message. Reads error text
literally. Notices untranslated strings, Japanese leaking into an
English page, and dates that are ambiguous because the format is not
stated.

### Two devices, interrupted work (`careless-multidevice`)

Identity: masters · Language: ja · Device: macos-arm64

Uses the desktop app on two machines with cloud backup enabled. Quits
mid-operation, sleeps the laptop, and lets the network drop.

Closes the window while something is still running. Reopens and expects
to see the result. Edits the same record on both machines on purpose.

### Narrow window, keyboard only (`narrow-window-keyboard`)

Identity: undergraduate · Language: en · Device: macos-arm64

Uses a small window on a laptop with an external monitor. Navigates by
keyboard and never touches the mouse.

Shrinks the window to its minimum size. Uses the number shortcuts and
Escape. Tabs through a form and expects focus to stay visible.

### Windows user snapping the desktop app (`windows-snap-user`)

Identity: undergraduate · Language: zh · Device: windows-x64

Uses the Windows desktop build on a laptop and keeps the app beside a
browser or course document using Windows Snap.

Expects the desktop navigation and the open course reader to stay usable
as the app moves between full-size, half-screen and quarter-screen sizes.

## Checks

### Real sign-in to the Science Tokyo portal and LMS (`SCHOOL-SIGNIN-SCIENCE`)

**Area** school · **Persona** 理工学系 1年生・初学期 · **Result** pass ⚠

> Needs re-running: covered paths changed after 7fdf1b6

**Preconditions**

Signed desktop bundle, campus network or VPN, a live student id and the
current OTP factor.

**Steps**

1. Cold-launch the bundle and wait for the first screen.
   - *Why:* Cold launch is where a stale keychain entry or a launch-order bug
     shows up; a warm relaunch hides both.
2. Open Settings → Accounts and connect the Science Tokyo account.
   Enter the student id, then the OTP when asked.
   - *Why:* The identity provider is tried first by design. Asking for a
     password before the id would mean the identity-first order regressed.
3. Wait for the badge, then open the LMS from the site list.
   - *Why:* Distinguishes "signed in" from "the session reaches the LMS". A badge
     that settles while the LMS still shows a login form is the failure
     this step exists to catch.
4. Look over the whole screen and the logs for the student id, the
   password or any OTP value.
   - *Why:* Credential material must never be rendered. A run that passes while
     leaking a value into the UI or a log is a failure.

**Where to look**

Settings → Accounts badge; the LMS page body; the app window and any
console output.

**Expected**

The account reaches Signed in without a second prompt, the LMS page
loads authenticated, and no credential material appears anywhere.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a real student id, a live OTP factor and the campus network. The
identity provider cannot be replayed offline and the OTP window makes a
recorded flow expire immediately.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/school_auth.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_browser/engine/**`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_service.rs`

**Last recorded** pass · 2026-10-14 · human · `7fdf1b6` · `1.0.0-rc.1`

Recorded in docs/verification/core-consolidation.md.

Evidence: `docs/verification/core-consolidation.md#live-macos-acceptance`

### Full LMS pull against a real account (`SCHOOL-LMS-PULL`)

**Area** school · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** pass ⚠

> Needs re-running: covered paths changed after 7fdf1b6

**Preconditions**

The account from SCHOOL-SIGNIN-SCIENCE is Signed in.

**Steps**

1. In a fresh disposable workspace, sign in and let the initial automatic
   full LMS pull finish. Then use Refresh now in the footer and verify
   it reads all courses, including quarters outside the current semester.
   - *Why:* The uninterrupted path establishes the baseline the interrupted path
     is compared against.
2. Compare courses and assignments with the authenticated LMS. Then
   reopen a previously cached lecture and press its Pull from LMS; keep
   reading while Core refreshes that course.
   - *Why:* A pull that "succeeds" with silently dropped courses is the failure
     this step catches; matching counts alone would not.
3. Open a visible school page in the middle of a second refresh.
   - *Why:* Sync reads go over HTTP and must neither stop nor wait for the
     visible page; a run that stalls until the page closes means a
     WebView dependency came back.
4. After a successful fresh pull, browse each available quarter and search
   its actual course codes in Lecture Desk and Today's cross-quarter
   course finder. Select a result, switch tabs, and use Filter's clear
   button. Open a Calendar course and a real linked subscription exam.
   - *Why:* Real LMS shortnames and syllabus details must retain searchable class
     codes and restore room metadata after setup. Calendar navigation must
     select the exact course or exam in its quarter without stale filters;
     do not manufacture an exam association when this account has no match.

**Where to look**

The LMS page course and assignment lists, the refresh timestamp, and the
visible school page that interrupted the second pull.

**Expected**

The first pull matches the LMS course list and advances its timestamp;
the lecture refresh reads that course only. Cached lecture content
remains usable during refresh and changed content produces one quiet,
short in-app update notice. Browsing a school page does not pause the
refresh.

**Why this is manual**

Depends on the authenticated Moodle session above. The AJAX surface is
read-only but account-scoped, so no fixture can stand in for a real
enrolment.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/lms_ingest.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/lms_session.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_parser/lms.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_parser/lms/pages.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/reader.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/ajax.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/catalog.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/data/school_projection.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/schedule/search.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/lectures/LectureDesk.tsx`

**Last recorded** pass · 2026-10-14 · human · `7fdf1b6` · `1.0.0-rc.1`

7 matched courses, no differences.

### LMS pull over the mobile token, and its fallback to the session cookie (`SCHOOL-LMS-TOKEN-PULL`)

**Area** school · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

The account from SCHOOL-SIGNIN-SCIENCE is Signed in, with at least one
course that has an assignment, a quiz and an announcement forum. A debug
desktop build with the app log visible.

**Steps**

1. With no LMS token in the vault (fresh profile, or after forgetting
   and re-adding the school account), run a full LMS pull.
   - *Why:* The token comes from one cookie-authenticated launch.php GET answered
     by a 302 to moodlemobile://; only the real site proves the redirect,
     the base64 layout and the md5(wwwroot + passport) signature agree
     with the parser.
2. Search the exported app log and the database file for the token's
   first characters (read them from the OS keychain item
   "lms-token-science" yourself; never paste the token anywhere).
   - *Why:* The token cannot be revoked by a student. A leak into a log, a row or
     an error message is the failure this step exists to catch.
3. Compare courses, assignment states (submitted, graded with grade,
   late-allowed), quiz states and announcement bodies with the LMS
   pages and with the previous cookie-based pull.
   - *Why:* Several REST functions (`mod_quiz_*`, `mod_forum_get_forums_by_courses`,
     the module getters, the calendar views, the timeline course list) are
     listed by the site but their answers were never probed. A silently
     empty mapping looks like "nothing to do" in Today.
4. Quit and restart the app, then pull the deadlines before opening any
   school page.
   - *Why:* The token survives the restart while the web session does not; the
     pull must not wait for a WebView sign-in except for the timetable.
5. Replace the keychain item's token with a random 32-character value and
   pull again.
   - *Why:* A refused token arrives as HTTP 200 with errorcode invalidtoken; the
     client must drop it, sign in once and launch a new one rather than
     loop or fall back silently forever.
6. Block `webservice/rest/server.php` (for example with a local proxy
   rule) and pull once more.
   - *Why:* The cookie transport must take over with the same results; the app
     log names the fallback reason without any credential.

**Where to look**

The LMS page lists, Today's assignment rows, the app log export and the
keychain item.

**Expected**

The first pull creates exactly one vault item and matches the LMS like
SCHOOL-LMS-PULL. No log line, database row or error contains the token,
sesskey or passport. After the restart the deadlines refresh before any
school page opens. The forged token is replaced after one sign-in and
the pull completes. With REST blocked the pull completes through the
cookie path with the same courses and states, and the log says the
token transport was unavailable.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a real account's web session to launch a token, and the answers of
account-scoped REST functions that no fixture can stand in for. The pure
parsing and mapping are covered by the net::moodle unit tests.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/mod.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/token.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/rest.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/moodle/ajax.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_auth.rs`
- `docs/lms-api/README.md`

**Last recorded** never run

### A first-year student is refused an upper-level course with a reason (`IDENTITY-FIRST-YEAR-GATE`)

**Area** identity · **Persona** 理工学系 1年生・初学期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

A study profile with the undergraduate stage and the current admission
year. A course placed at a level above that stage.

**Steps**

1. Open the planner and search for a course only open to later years.
   - *Why:* Establishes what the app shows before any action: a row that is
     offered at all is the precondition for testing the refusal.
2. Try to add it, by clicking and by pasting its course code.
   - *Why:* Both paths must be gated. A refusal on one path and a silent accept
     on the other is the classic version of this bug.
3. Read the text of the refusal.
   - *Why:* "Cannot add" with no reason is a failure for this persona: the check
     is about whether the app explains the rule, not whether it blocks.

**Where to look**

The planner result row, the add buttons and their tooltips, and the
notification or inline message the refusal produces.

**Expected**

Every add path is refused or disabled, and the message names the rule
(the study stage or year the course requires) rather than only failing.

**Why this is manual**

The rule itself is unit-tested, but whether a student understands the
refusal is a judgement about wording and placement that only a rendered
screen can show.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/study_profile.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/course_query/mod.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/courses/**`

### 教務Web registration and requirements pages import or report unavailable (`SCHOOL-KYOMU-REGISTRATION-REQUIREMENTS`)

**Area** school · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

Signed desktop bundle, Tokyo Tech account Signed in, campus network or
VPN. Run once inside a 科目申告 window and once outside it. Outside the
window was observed passing on 2026-10-17 (state 本登録済); the window
itself, where courses are still being edited, is not yet observed.

**Steps**

1. Quit the app, then start it from a terminal so stderr is kept:
   `/Applications/IsctCompanion.app/Contents/MacOS/isct-companion 2>&1 | tee artifacts/kyomu-pull.log`
   - *Why:* Partial page failures are only reported to stderr, which a bundle
     launched from Finder discards. Without this the run gives no reason
     for the failure, as happened on 2026-10-17.
2. Use the manual 教務Web refresh and wait until the footer settles.
   - *Why:* Manual refresh bypasses the retry backoff, so the run reaches the
     registration (PID1_0) and requirements (PID2_6) pages now.
3. Find the `[school-pull] Kyomu/registrations:` and
   `[school-pull] Kyomu/requirements:` lines in the log and copy the
   text after `kyomu extraction was incomplete:`.
   - *Why:* That text is the extractor check that rejected the page. On
     2026-10-17 it was a header-less empty unit GridView
     (`kamokuUnit_-2_gvKamoku`) and a requirement table whose header has
     no <thead>; both are now read. A new reason names the next shape.
4. Open both pages in the visible 教務Web view. Read the page's notice,
   if any, and inspect the element that holds it (its id or class).
   Check whether the elements named in the log line exist.
   - *Why:* Decides the fix. If the page shows a notice such as "outside the
     申告 period", the extractor's unavailable pattern must learn that
     notice and its element. If the data is visible but the selector
     does not match, the selector is broken.
5. Run `sqlite3 -readonly "$HOME/Library/Application Support/app.isctcompanion/cache.db" "SELECT key,outcome,fetched_at,failures,last_error FROM dataset_state WHERE dataset='kyomu.page'"`.
   - *Why:* Only a complete read sets `fetched_at`, with outcome `complete` or
     `unavailable`. A page without one stays due and backs off after
     each failure, recorded in `failures` and `last_error`.

**Where to look**

artifacts/kyomu-pull.log, the two 教務Web pages in the visible view, and
the dataset_state query output.

**Expected**

`registrations` and `requirements` each have a `fetched_at` with outcome
`complete` or `unavailable`, the log has no `school-pull` line for either page,
and the footer no longer shows a 教務Web failure after a refresh.

**Why this is manual**

The live registration and requirement DOM is account-scoped and changes
with the 申告 window. No automated test reads a real 教務Web page and no
committed fixture is a capture. Only a real session shows what the
portal serves while registration is open.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/net/kyomu.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_parser/kyomu/pages.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_parser/kyomu.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/kyomu_ingest.rs`

that cannot be automated without live credentials.

### Campus-card OCR on a physical card (`OCR-CAMPUS-CARD`)

**Area** ocr · **Persona** 理工学系 1年生・初学期 · **Result** pass ⚠

> Needs re-running: covered paths changed after 7fdf1b6

**Preconditions**

A supported desktop target with OCR, a physical campus card, and a
camera or a photo of the card.

**Steps**

1. Open the matrix OCR flow and supply a photo of a real card.
   - *Why:* Synthetic tensors and the frozen filter fixture cover the pipeline
     stage by stage; a real card is what exposes lighting, angle and
     printing variation that no fixture reproduces.
2. Open Scan with camera in a packaged desktop app, allow camera access,
   and bring the real card toward the camera. Check that one red outline
   follows the Matrix, with no cell boxes or letter overlays. Move the
   card, introduce glare, then briefly hold it steady with labels visible.
   Observe the per-cell acquisition coverage. The camera must stop as
   soon as every cell has enough clear candidates, or within eight seconds
   of the first detected Matrix; waiting before detection does not count.
   After acquisition, the dialog closes, the camera indicator turns off,
   and inline processing progress appears. Put the card down and verify
   results arrive; insufficient votes must be highlighted for review.
   Repeat with the card rotated 90, 180 and 270 degrees. Each orientation
   must keep the same cell order. If processing produces no readable
   letters, it must show a retryable error without reopening the stopped
   camera or returning to a 70/70 capture loop.
   Inspect matrix-scan/latest.json under the app cache for separate
   acquisition/processing times, per-cell candidate and qualified-vote
   counts. Use an optimized build and move the framed card continuously:
   the red outline must update at least 10 times per second (30 preferred).
   Check frameMs and frames/elapsedMs alongside the visible tracking;
   a smoothly interpolated stale outline does not count as a new detection.
   Compare all 70 letters with the real card.
   - *Why:* OS camera permissions, native WebView video capture, optical focus,
     and the alignment of recognition boxes over a physical card require
     real hardware. Scripted frames cannot validate these surfaces.
3. Start fresh camera sessions with a readable card under backlighting,
   uneven shadow and a moving reflection. Confirm the first red outline
   appears and acquisition starts. Move the card slightly so the reflection
   leaves each cell; unobscured cells must retain their progress. Hold a
   bright reflection over the same letters until the deadline and check
   that erased strokes remain marked for review rather than accepted.
   Include a white card background and modest hand movement.
   After closing each session, inspect core.geometryFrames,
   core.admissionRejections and core.glareRejections in
   matrix-scan/latest.json, then compare all accepted letters with the card.
   - *Why:* Real camera exposure, sensor noise and specular reflections can differ
     from synthetic lighting. Hardware is needed to check initial admission,
     false glare on white paper and recovery as a reflection moves.
4. Cancel and reopen the camera, then background the app during capture.
   Repeat and background it during processing: acquisition stops in the
   former case, but the latter may finish without reopening the camera.
   Cancel processing and confirm late results do not overwrite the editor.
   Deny permission on a fresh permission state and retry after granting it.
   - *Why:* Verify the camera indicator switches off and permissions can recover
     in the signed native app; headless tests cannot observe OS resource
     release or the native privacy prompt.
5. Review the recognised cells and compare them with the card.
   - *Why:* The contract is "no wrong accepted cell", not "most cells right". A
     misread cell that is accepted is worse than a rejected one, so the
     comparison has to be cell by cell.
6. Correct a cell and save.
   - *Why:* Confirms the manual correction path, which the fixtures never take.

**Where to look**

The recognised cell grid beside the physical card, and the saved values.

**Expected**

Every expected cell is recognised, no wrong cell is accepted, and the
corrected values are what get saved.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a physical card and a camera. Intel Mac builds ship without the
OCR runtime, so the target must be chosen deliberately.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-ocr/**`
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/matrix-ocr.ts`
- `crates/isct-core/src/matrix_scan.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/matrix_scan/**`
- `apps/desktop/src/platform/matrix-camera.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/components/MatrixCamera.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/components/matrix-camera.css`
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/settings/SchoolAccounts.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/matrix_camera.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Info.plist`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Entitlements.plist`

**Last recorded** pass · 2026-10-14 · human · `7fdf1b6` · `1.0.0-rc.1`

67 expected cells recognised, no wrong accepted cells; private image not committed.

### Desktop MCP endpoint against a real client (`DESKTOP-MCP-LIVE`)

**Area** desktop · **Persona** Narrow window, keyboard only · **Result** pass ⚠

> Needs re-running: covered paths changed after 7fdf1b6

**Preconditions**

A built desktop app and a real MCP client.

**Steps**

1. Enable AI agent access, copy the token, and point the client at
   http://127.0.0.1:47832/mcp.
   - *Why:* Initialization and the tool list are negotiated by the client, not
     by our tests; a real client is the only way to see that handshake.
2. Read today and the schedule through the client and compare with the
   app window.
   - *Why:* The point of the endpoint is parity with the UI. A read that differs
     from the window would go unnoticed by a protocol-only test.
3. Retry with a wrong token and with a hostile Origin header, then
   check the token file's permissions.
   - *Why:* Authorization and file mode are the security boundary; 401, 403 and
     mode 0600 must all hold together.

**Where to look**

The client's initialization and tool list, the values it reads beside
the app window, the HTTP status of each retry, and the token file mode.

**Expected**

Initialization and the tool list succeed, the reads match the app, the
wrong token returns 401, the hostile Origin returns 403, and the token
file stays mode 0600.

**Why this is manual**

Confirming a real client negotiates the protocol and that the OS file
mode holds needs the built app.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/agent_server.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/agent/**`

### Fast navigation while a live LMS pull lands data (`DESKTOP-PULL-STRESS`)

**Area** desktop · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

A development build started with `VITE_INTERACTION_TRACE=1 yarn
desktop:dev`, the account from SCHOOL-SIGNIN-SCIENCE signed in, and at
least two quarters that have courses, one of them with open assignments.

**Steps**

1. Confirm the dev terminal prints `[trace] recording to
   tmp/interaction-trace/…`.
   - *Why:* A crash found by hand is only useful if the steps before it can be
     read back. The 2026-10-16 Lecture Desk crash looked random until its
     timeline showed the quarter change that triggered it.
2. Start a full LMS pull. While it runs, open several lectures in quick
   succession, toggle Lectures and Assignments, change the quarter in
   both modes, and jump to Home and Web and back.
   - *Why:* Each ingest publishes a new revision while revision-keyed queries
     refetch, so a view that joins two queries can render with one
     answered and the other still loading. That only happens when an
     ingest lands in the middle of input, which no scripted run times.
3. Keep going until the trace shows at least two `school-ingest` events
   that arrived between your clicks.
   - *Why:* One ingest can fall into a pause between clicks and prove nothing.
     The trace, not a feeling of having clicked enough, decides when the
     overlap actually happened.
4. After the pull ends, compare Lectures (both modes, every quarter) and
   Home with the same pages after a cold relaunch.
   - *Why:* The quieter failure is a view that survives but keeps the rows it
     skipped while data was loading. Work hidden during a load has to
     reappear once its course arrives.

**Where to look**

Every page for "This page hit an error"; the dev terminal for `[trace]`
error blocks; `error`, `rejected` and `console.error` entries in the
newest tmp/interaction-trace/*.jsonl.

**Expected**

No page error and no error entries in the trace; after the pull, each
page matches the cold relaunch.

**Why this is manual**

The interleaving comes from a real, account-scoped LMS pull meeting
human input at real timing. The e2e harness scripts revisions but not
that race. A failure found here that reproduces deterministically moves
into a suite, as the quarter-switch case did in
tests/e2e/today-and-lectures.test.tsx.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src/store/workspace.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/platform/core-query.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/useSync.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/lectures/LectureDesk.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/interaction-trace.ts`

### Native shells on physical devices (`NATIVE-DEVICE-FLOWS`)

**Area** native · **Persona** 理工学系 1年生・初学期 · **Result** **unreached**

> Not verified: unreached: The SwiftUI and Compose shells do not exist yet.

**Preconditions**

A signed build, provisioning, and physical iOS and Android devices.

**Steps**

1. Install the build on each device and complete first-run.
   - *Why:* Installation and the OS authorization prompts are outside anything
     the repository can simulate.
2. On an iPhone signed in to the same Apple ID as a Mac whose desktop
   app is already connected, open 設定 → 学校アカウント before typing
   anything.
   - *Why:* School logins are synchronized iCloud Keychain items named by Core
     (`vault_item`). Showing 未接続 here means the iOS item identity or
     access group drifted from the desktop's.
3. Walk sign-in, pull to refresh on 今日, the ウェブ tab, a course's
   LMS link, hiding an assignment, and turning on reminders.
   - *Why:* The native shells render independently of the desktop frontend, so
     desktop acceptance says nothing about them. Pulls run through the
     WKWebView browser port, which only a real identity provider and OTP
     exercise.
4. On Android, sign in from 設定, pull to refresh on 今日, open the
   ウェブ tab and a course's LMS link, swipe an assignment to hide
   it, then turn on reminders and wait for one to arrive.
   - *Why:* Pulls run through the WebView browser port and Core's injected
     scripts, which only a real identity provider and OTP exercise;
     reminders depend on the notification permission and alarm delivery
     of a real device.
5. On iOS, pull down on 今日 and watch the ring beside the settings
   button, then tap it.
   - *Why:* The ring and the sheet render Core's sync snapshot
     (`sync_engine`), the same value as the desktop footer. A ring shown
     for a run without a total, or a sheet whose LMS and 教務Web rows
     disagree with the desktop footer, means the shell stopped following
     Core.
6. On iOS, open a course from a timetable block, switch to 資料 and open
   a PDF; then tap the timetable title, pick another quarter's chip and
   a week in the list.
   - *Why:* Files download with the resident web view's sign-in (the cookie
     port) into the folder desktop uses; a Safari hand-off or a login
     prompt means the port or the folder name drifted. The picker labels
     come from Core's `TimetableYear`; a quarter chip that lands on a
     week outside that quarter means the jump target is wrong.
7. On an iPad, hold it upright, then turn it to landscape, open 授業 and
   pick two courses.
   - *Why:* Upright keeps the tab bar with 授業 added; landscape switches to the
     sidebar and the course list beside the course page, by the desktop's
     width rule. A course page that does not change, or a back stack that
     survives choosing another course, means the split lost its owner.
8. On each device, after a pull, turn two reminder switches on in quick
   succession, force-quit the app, reopen it and open 設定.
   - *Why:* Each account row's 更新 time comes from Core's school status; a time
     that disappears after the restart means the shell went back to its
     own clock. Both switches staying on shows settings edits are applied
     one after another, as on desktop, instead of the second copying
     stale settings.

**Where to look**

Each device's screens, its authorization prompts, and the notifications
it delivers.

**Expected**

The flows work with the platform's own UI, authorization prompts and
notification delivery; school pages open inside the app, never in
Safari, and a pull fills 今日 and 課題.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a real student id and OTP, iCloud Keychain on two devices, signing
and provisioning for physical hardware.

**Covers**

- `apps/android/**`
- `apps/ios/**`
- `bindings/**`
- `crates/isct-ffi/**`

**Area** desktop · **Persona** Narrow window, keyboard only · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

An updated native desktop build (on macOS, launch the packaged .app) and
OS notification permission available. Disable Focus for the banner check.
Stop screen sharing/mirroring, or allow notifications while sharing.

**Steps**

1. On macOS, launch with yarn desktop:dev and open Notifications. Then
   build with yarn desktop:build --debug --bundles app, launch that
   packaged .app and click Allow notifications or Send. For
   first-time permission, accept the system prompt; for a previously
   denied permission, use Open notification settings to allow the app,
   then return. Toggle permission in System Settings and return again.
   - *Why:* The bare development executable cannot use UserNotifications. It must
     report that limitation without persisting a refusal or claiming that
     System Settings blocked the app. The packaged app must ask when
     undetermined, link to settings when denied, and refresh the real OS
     permission on return instead of trusting a stale saved value. Its
     local bundle signature must use app.isctcompanion so macOS can match
     it to the notification authorization.
2. On both macOS and Windows, open Settings > Notifications, click Test
   notification, then click the native banner while the app is behind
   another window.
   - *Why:* A successful command is not enough: this checks actual OS delivery
     and that the native activation callback returns focus to the app.
3. Grant notification permission, enable class, exam and assignment reminders,
   and choose a separate non-default lead time for each type.
   - *Why:* Real OS consent and notification delivery are unavailable to the
     headless settings and reminder-plan tests.
4. In a disposable local workspace, arrange a class, a linked subscription
   exam and an assignment so their reminder times occur shortly. Turn class
   reminders off while leaving exam reminders on, then background the app.
   - *Why:* Verifies that native lifecycle wakeups deliver the selected times
     even when the settings page and the application window are inactive.

**Where to look**

The operating system notification centre and the selected reminder times
in Settings > Notifications after reopening the page.

**Expected**

The development executable explains that notification permission needs
the packaged app. In the .app, the permission status follows System
Settings without restarting. The test notification shows a banner both
in foreground and background, and clicking it focuses the app. Each
scheduled native notification arrives while the app process remains
running, with the correct exam or assignment title; the disabled class
reminder stays silent, and selected times remain saved.

**Why this is manual**

Requires actual OS notification permission, background lifecycle callbacks
and native notification delivery; tests use a headless notification sink.

the app and its data. A debug build may use the strictly loopback fixture
origin; release builds always use the source repository.

**Steps**

   - *Why:* Cocoa's predefined Quit can bypass ExitRequested; the native menu must enter owned shutdown before installing verified bytes.

**Expected**

Tampered content is rejected, the valid bundle installs through Cmd-Q,
the new version reopens and saved data and login credentials remain.
A source repository with no stable release is reported as unpublished.

**Why this is manual**

Requires Developer ID signing, real macOS menu dispatch, Keychain access and native app-bundle replacement.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/desktop_updates.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`

### Windows updates download on a slow link and report the install result (`DESKTOP-WINDOWS-UPDATES`)

**Area** desktop · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

An installed Windows release built from this source with the updater key,
a newer signed release published, and a Windows PC whose Smart App
Control can be switched between Off and On (or a second PC with it On).

**Steps**

1. Throttle the connection to about 2 Mbps (e.g. a metered hotspot or a router limit), open Settings > About and press Download update.
   - *Why:* The installer is over 30 MB; only a real slow link shows whether the download outlives the old 30-second whole-request timeout and whether the byte counter moves while the command is still running.
2. Disconnect the network mid-download and wait about a minute.
   - *Why:* A stalled transfer must end in an error that names the stall, not leave the panel on "Downloading" forever.
3. With Smart App Control Off, press Install and quit, let the NSIS installer finish and reopen the app.
   - *Why:* On Windows the process exits before the installer runs, so the success notice depends on the next launch comparing versions. Quitting drains background work for up to 15 seconds; a window left on screen meanwhile looks frozen.
4. Repeat the install with Smart App Control On.
   - *Why:* Smart App Control blocks the unsigned installer after the app has exited; only a real policy shows what the next launch reports.

**Where to look**

Settings > About status line, the notice at launch, and the version shown in About.

**Expected**

The About line shows "Downloading update… · x / y MB" with x increasing,
and the download completes on the slow link. A disconnect ends in
"Update check failed · The update download stopped receiving data…".
The window disappears as soon as Install and quit is pressed. After a
successful install the app reopens on the new version with
"Updated to <version>." After a blocked install the old version opens
with a red notice saying the update did not install, and About repeats it.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a signed release on GitHub, a Windows PC, a real slow or broken network, and the Smart App Control policy, none of which a headless test can provide.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/desktop_updates.rs`

- `apps/desktop/src/app/useDesktopUpdates.ts`

### Every database write reaches the window and the cloud on its own (`DESKTOP-WRITES-PUBLISH-THEMSELVES`)

**Area** desktop · **Persona** Two devices, interrupted work · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

macOS desktop app signed in to Science Tokyo, Google Drive backup
enabled with automatic sync on, AI agent access enabled with a real MCP
client connected, and a second device signed in to the same Drive.

**Steps**

1. Open the Web tab, browse to an LMS course page with an assignment
   that is not yet in the app, then switch to the Assignments page
   without pressing refresh.
   - *Why:* A page opened by the person is ingested by Core, not by a pull. That
     ingest used to commit without publishing, so the window kept the old
     list until something else reloaded it.
2. From the MCP client, create a plan event for tomorrow, then look at
   the Calendar in the app window.
   - *Why:* The desktop agent server no longer emits the change itself; Core's
     commit path must publish it with source mcp.
3. Edit a plan in the app, save a course note, then watch the cloud
   sync status and open the other device about ten seconds later.
   - *Why:* The shell no longer captures right after a mutation or note save.
     Core brings the next capture forward and the one-second wake runs
     it; a missing request would leave the edit unsynced for the whole
     interval or until the next foreground.
4. Import a local backup from Settings, then reset the workspace and
   import it again.
   - *Why:* Restore and reset replace many rows in one commit and used to rely
     on the shell's capture; the window must show the result and the
     cloud must receive it without a manual sync.
5. Clear the school cache in Settings, open Today and leave the window
   alone while the first pull refills it; then open Courses, Grades and
   the course finder.
   - *Why:* A background commit now patches only the records its change names
     feed, read against real LMS and 教務 rows. A table mapped to the
     wrong name would leave one of these pages on the old data until the
     app restarts, which no fixture shows.

**Where to look**

The Assignments list, the Calendar, Today, Courses, Grades, the finder,
the Settings cloud sync status and the second device's copy of the
edited plan and note.

**Expected**

The new assignment and the MCP event appear without a refresh, the
edited plan and the note reach the second device within a few seconds,
both the import and the reset show in the window and upload without
pressing Sync, and after the refill every page shows the pulled data
without navigating away and back.

**Why this is manual**

The visible-page ingest needs a signed-in LMS page in the real WebView,
the MCP step needs a real client, and the capture timing needs a real
cloud provider and a second device. Core tests prove that each commit is
published and brings capture forward; only the built app shows that the
shell, which no longer does either, still gets there.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/workspace.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lms_files.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/agent_server.rs`

### iPhone course page turns lessons by swipe, as one piece, both ways (`IOS-COURSE-LESSON-PAGING`)

**Area** native · **Persona** 理工学系 1年生・初学期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

The iPhone app with LMS content pulled for a course whose LMS numbers at
least three lessons (第1回, 第2回, …), at least one with 授業計画 text.

**Steps**

1. Open the course from 時間割 and swipe left across the lesson card,
   then right.
   - *Why:* The pager must turn to the next lesson on a left swipe and back on a
     right one; the old page leaves toward the side the finger moved and
     the new one comes from the other. A transition fixed to one edge
     made "previous" look like "next".
2. Watch the card with the 授業計画 text as it moves in.
   - *Why:* The text used to arrive after the card (a progress placeholder, then
     the rendered HTML), so the card grew and its text slid separately.
     It must arrive at full height and move with its background.
3. Drag slowly a little under a third of the width and let go; then
   flick quickly a short distance.
   - *Why:* A slow short drag springs back; a flick over 300 pt/s turns the
     page. Either rule breaking makes paging feel random.
4. On the first lesson drag right; on the last drag left.
   - *Why:* At an end there is only a damped pull, never a turn.
5. Start a swipe at the very left edge of the screen.
   - *Why:* Edge drags belong to the navigation back gesture; the page must pop
     back to the timetable rather than turn a lesson.
6. Scroll the page vertically with a slightly diagonal drag, and tap a
   file row.
   - *Why:* The pager runs alongside scrolling and taps; a drag that starts
     vertical stays a scroll for its whole length.

**Where to look**

The course page pushed from 時間割.

**Expected**

Lessons turn in the direction of the swipe, each page moves as one piece
with its text already laid out, ends only rubber-band, the edge swipe
pops, and scrolling and taps work as before.

**Why this is manual**

Gesture feel and animation are judged by eye on a phone; an e2e test over
a fake host would rebuild the screen rather than test it.

### iPhone and Mac load each other's data through one iCloud record (`IOS-ICLOUD-BACKUP`)

**Area** cloud · **Persona** Two devices, interrupted work · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

The released (Developer ID) Mac app and the iPhone app, both signed with
the team that owns `iCloud.app.isctcompanion`, on one Apple Account. The
iPhone build carries the Production container environment, so both read
the same CloudKit database.

**Steps**

1. On the Mac, Settings → Backup: turn on iCloud and Upload. On the
   iPhone, 設定 › バックアップ: turn on iCloud and Pull.
   - *Why:* The phone must load the Mac's plans, notes and hidden assignments.
     Nothing arriving usually means the two builds use different CloudKit
     environments or containers, not a merge bug.
2. On the iPhone hide an assignment and Upload; on the Mac Pull.
   - *Why:* The reverse direction goes through the phone's CloudKitStore write;
     a refused or partial write shows as an iCloud error on the phone.
3. Without pulling first, edit a different record on each device, then
   Upload on both.
   - *Why:* The second upload must lose CloudKit's conditional save, re-read and
     merge. Losing either edit means a write replaced a record it had not
     read.
4. On the iPhone, open 以前のバージョン and restore one; then export a
   backup file on the Mac and import it on the phone with 読み込む….
   - *Why:* Restore and import both start a new generation on every device and
     leave a local recovery file; the Mac must follow on its next Pull.

**Where to look**

The Backup pages on both devices (provider line, versions, recovery
files) and the records themselves on each.

**Expected**

Each device shows the other's changes after a Pull, both concurrent edits
survive, the version list names both devices, and a restore or import on
the phone reaches the Mac with a recovery file kept on each.

**Why this is manual**

CloudKit needs a signed build, an iCloud account and a device; the
merge, tag-conditional write and journal behind it are covered by
`sessions_sharing_one_cloud_record_load_each_others_data` and
`tagged_writes_carry_the_tag_read_with_the_expected_revision`.

**Covers**

- `apps/ios/IsctCompanion/Core/CloudKitStore.swift`
- `apps/ios/IsctCompanion/Features/Settings/BackupScreen.swift`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/icloud.rs`

### 教務Web pages load over Rust HTTP on every platform (`SCHOOL-KYOMU-RUST-TLS`)

**Area** school · **Persona** 理工学系 3年生・履修計画期 · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

A build where 教務Web pages are read by Core's HTTP client (sync-engine
checkpoint 3 or later), saved Tokyo Tech credentials, and one of macOS, Windows,
iPhone or Android (repeat per platform).

**Steps**

1. Sign in to 教務Web in the app, then refresh 教務Web data from
   Settings.
   - *Why:* kyomu0 sends the wrong intermediate certificate. Apple and Windows
     may repair the chain on their own, Android does not, so only a run on
     each platform shows the vendored G7 intermediate is what makes it work.
2. Open the 教務Web page in the app's school browser afterwards.
   - *Why:* Cookies the server set on Core's requests are written back to the
     WebView store; a broken write-back shows up as the browser being
     signed out or bounced to GetAccess.
3. Leave the app idle for at least an hour (the 教務Web session expires
   while GetAccess stays signed in), then press Retry or refresh
   教務Web once.
   - *Why:* A live GetAccess sign-in is not a 教務Web session; only the hidden
     view opening the 教務 entry page starts a new one, which no test can
     drive without the school's sign-on.

**Where to look**

The 教務Web status in Settings, the application log, and the school
browser page.

**Expected**

All six 教務Web pages refresh with no TLS error in the log, and the
school browser opens 教務Web still signed in. After the idle hour the
log shows one `kyomu entry result=Ok(true)` per refresh and the pages
refresh, not a run of TokyoTech session checks ending in sign-in
failures.

**Why this is manual**

Needs a real Tokyo Tech account and the real kyomu0 certificate chain on
each OS verifier; no test can reach the school server.

**Covers**

- `crates/isct-core/src/net/tls.rs`
- `crates/isct-core/src/net/certs/nii-odca4g7rsa.pem`
- `crates/isct-core/src/school_browser/engine/login.rs`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lms_downloader.rs`
- `apps/ios/IsctCompanion/Core/WebCookieSession.swift`

### Clear school caches and resync, and Full reset, from Settings → Backup (`SETTINGS-RESET`)

**Area** desktop · **Persona** Two devices, interrupted work · **Result** —

> Not verified: never verified

**Preconditions**

The desktop app signed in to Science Tokyo with saved credentials, school
data synced (Today, assignments, 教務Web grades, course search all
populated), at least one downloaded course file and one course note, one
plan and one hidden assignment, and iCloud or Google Drive sync on with a
recent upload.

**Steps**

1. Settings → バックアップ → 「学校のキャッシュを消去して再同期」 → 消去…;
   read the panel, tick both options, then press 消去して再同期.
   - *Why:* The panel must list what goes and what stays, and the two options
     must move "school web sign-in" and "downloaded course files" from
     the kept list to the deleted list. A missing or zero size estimate
     means the preview command or `dbstat` failed.
2. While it runs, look at the refresh buttons and the status line;
   press the open button again.
   - *Why:* During a reset the refresh buttons show リセット中… from the
     snapshot's `resetting` flag, and a second press cannot start a
     second reset.
3. Open Today, Assignments and the course search, then a course with
   the downloaded file and its notes.
   - *Why:* The views must show the empty state with cold-start progress and
     then refill; the plan, the hidden assignment's mark and the notes
     must still be there; the file card must read "not downloaded" and
     download again on open; the school browser must sign in again with
     the saved credentials before LMS data arrives.
4. Settings → バックアップ → 「完全リセット」 → リセット…; check that この端末を
   リセット stays disabled until the confirmation box is ticked; choose
   クラウドから復元する and confirm.
   - *Why:* A full reset deletes user data, settings and saved logins; the
     extra confirmation and the cloud question are the only guard. With
     restore chosen, the plan and the hidden assignment must come back
     from the cloud copy, while school data resyncs only after signing in
     again.
5. On the second device, Pull.
   - *Why:* A reset must not write tombstones: the second device must keep every
     plan, mark and note.

**Where to look**

Settings → Backup (panel, buttons, the notice after each reset), the
status line, Today / Assignments / course search, a course page's files
and notes, Settings → School accounts, and the second device.

**Expected**

Clearing keeps plans, marks, notes and saved logins, deletes downloaded
files and the web sign-in, and resyncs everything; the course folder's
notes are untouched. Full reset returns to first launch, restores the
user data from the cloud when asked, and the second device loses
nothing.

**Why this is manual**

The WebView cookie store, the course folder on disk, real school sign-in
and a cloud provider cannot be driven headless. What each scope deletes,
the lease, the generation and the downloads purge are covered by
`crates/isct-core/src/tests/reset.rs`; this check is the shell wiring
and what a person sees.

**Covers**

- `apps/desktop/src/pages/settings/ResetSettings.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/reset.rs`

**Last recorded** never run
